prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Looking steeply downward from the head-mounted camera, the depth map captures the vertical distance hierarchy from the camera wearer's bright white protruding torso at 0.1–0.4 m below the lens, down along the mid-grey arms and hands gripping the lawnmower handlebar within arm's reach at roughly 0.5–0.7 m, to the darker mower grass bag and engine deck stretching 0.8–1.5 m ahead over the dark ground plane (~1.5–1.7 m away). No other people are present, and the wearer faces forward along the mower's path while their torso occludes their legs except for the stepping left foot in frame 1 and right leg in frames 3–5 protruding beneath the handlebar. Across the five frames, the relative depth between the wearer and the lawnmower stays constant as both advance together and turn slightly rightward in frames 4–5, while the front edge of the mower deck touches the top frame boundary in frames 3 and 5. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the 3D elevation step between the raised handlebar assembly, the mid-level grass catcher bag, and the flat lawn surface beneath much clearer, as well as the forward extension of the lower leg under the handlebar in frames 3–5. However, the map is unreliable along the thin side support rods of the handlebar, which intermittently merge into the background lawn depth, and near the outer frame vignettes where the flat sidewalk on the left and bushes on the right lose distinct depth contrast.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground region occupied by the camera wearer's torso and outstretched arms (0.1–0.7 m from the camera, facing forward with no other people in the scene) at the bottom of all five frames, along with parts of the lawnmower 0.8–1.5 m ahead in front of the wearer and the curved concrete walkway ~0.8–1.5 m to the left in frame 3. Across the sequence, the wearer's hands remain in contact with the handlebar within arm's reach while their torso occludes the lower body, and the leftward sidewalk shifts out of frame as the wearer turns right in frames 4 and 5. While this map helps separate the silhouette of the wearer's upper body and arms from the textured grass background, its semantic labels and masks are highly unreliable under this steep egocentric viewpoint. Specifically, it misclassifies the lawnmower's deck and grass bag as a 'person' in frames 1 and 5 and as a 'parking meter' in frames 2 and 3, completely misses the mower in frame 4, and mislabels the left concrete sidewalk in frame 3 as a 'surfboard'. Furthermore, the handlebar and the wearer's hands are fragmented or omitted into the black background, and the wearer's torso and the mower are inconsistently split into multiple overlapping 'person' instances in frames 1–3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal locations of the camera wearer's left and right hands (magenta) gripping the lawnmower handlebar within arm's reach at roughly 0.5–0.7 m in front of and below the camera, while confirming no other people are present or facing the wearer. Across the five frames, the hand skeletons record the slight rightward steering rotation of the handlebar—with the right hand shifting slightly higher and further forward than the left hand in frame 5—as the wearer pushes the mower forward and turns right. Compared to the RGB image, the magenta hand skeletons isolate the exact finger curl and wrist orientation around the grips without distraction from the surrounding mower controls. However, the map is largely unreliable for tracking full-body spatial layout from a top-down egocentric angle because the wearer's protruding chest occludes the lower body and the head-mounted viewpoint truncates the upper torso. Consequently, the left hand is missed entirely in frames 2 and 3, the body skeleton (yellow) is absent in four of the five frames, and in frame 4 the estimator hallucinates an inverted, narrow yellow torso-and-limb skeleton over the wearer's chest and visible right leg.
